    //==
    // # Named colors - the 141 CSS Color Module Level 4 / X11 names
    //
    // The named-color table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_colors): 141 CSS
    // Color Module Level 4 / X11 names as `Color8` constants. The `Color` arithmetic
    // is in the section above.
    //
    // COLOR SPACE - read before using the named colors. The CSS/X11 names are defined
    // as **8-bit sRGB** (gamma-encoded) values, so they are declared here on `Color8`,
    // whose doc comment already states it is "typically sRGB-encoded". They are NOT
    // `Color` values: `Color` is LINEAR-light RGBA, and NO transfer-function conversion
    // happens anywhere in this section. To obtain a linear `Color` from one of these
    // constants you must decode explicitly through the sRGB transfer function - the
    // `TransferFunction`/`ColorSRGB` vocabulary in `color-spaces.types.plato` owns that
    // conversion. Treating a Color8 constant as if it were linear light will visibly
    // wash out any blending, filtering, or lighting done with it.
    //
    // Alpha: the CSS/X11 table defines RGB only; every constant here is fully opaque
    // (A = 255).
    //
    // Constants follow the tree-wide idiom of dispatching on an ignored receiver of the
    // result type, so they read as `Color8.AliceBlue` (see `constants.library.plato`).

    //==
    // Values are 8-bit sRGB (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRGB), fully opaque.
    // Read as `Color8.CornflowerBlue`. Exact duplicates in the standard are
    // preserved as separate names (Aqua = Cyan, Fuchsia = Magenta) because both
    // spellings are in the spec.

    // sRGB (240, 248, 255), opaque.
    AliceBlue(_: Color8): Color8
        => (240, 248, 255, 255);
